name: Vesoma 1
description: A bipedal humanoid from Vesoma, a European startup based in Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus — built around a self-improving reinforcement-learning approach in which the robot learns to move by trial and error rather than by imitating human demonstrations. Lab prototypes already walk using a self-learned policy.
sourcing: Company and product details sourced from Vesoma's own site (vesoma.com), its "Introducing Vesoma" announcement (September 22, 2026), and third-party coverage (Dealroom, Humanoids Daily, RobotsBeat, The Humanoid Hub) as of September 2026. No hardware specs (height, weight, DOF, battery, sensors) have been published by the company; the image used here is Vesoma's own design rendering, cleaned of a third-party aggregator's watermark before use — it is not photography of built hardware, and only lab prototypes are known to exist. Moved directly to Under Review (pending) at initial listing given the product's pre-production stage. robotindex does not sell this product.

pricing.summary: Not announced. Vesoma has not published a price, and no unit is for sale — only lab prototypes currently exist.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: Vesoma has not published sensor, actuator, battery, or dimensional specifications for Vesoma 1. The company's stated focus is its AI approach rather than a particular hardware bill of materials: its prototypes reportedly went from initial design to a working, self-learned walking policy within about six months.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Vesoma was founded in December 2025 by Nikolai Ensslen (co-founder of motion-control company Synapticon) and Peter Skoromnyi (co-founder of mobile-games company Easybrain), and exited stealth on September 22, 2026 with a team already past 60 people. Its AI research is led by Martin Riedmiller, formerly a research director and Control Team lead at Google DeepMind. The company's pitch is a "physical general intelligence" approach: instead of training on human demonstrations like most humanoid programs, Vesoma's robots learn by exploring and failing in the real world. First target markets are manufacturing, logistics, and warehousing; Vesoma has also stated its technology is not for weapons, military, or surveillance use. The image on Vesoma's own homepage is explicitly labeled a design rendering, not a photo of built hardware — only lab prototypes exist as of this writing.

firmwareCommunity.note: Vesoma has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
